prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Tennis kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the shirt, laid flat and face up
- the shorts below it
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.
- the ball or implement of Tennis
- the WRISTBAND and the HEADBAND laid flat side by side in the empty space beside the kit — each its own separate item, never on top of another garment

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: A WHITE short-sleeved tennis POLO exactly as photo2.png shows it — the body of it plain WHITE, which is correct and is NOT a contradiction of his TURQUOISE club colour: turquoise is carried by the TRIM. A turquoise FOLD-OVER polo COLLAR edged with a fine white line — a normal turned-down polo collar, not a stand collar; a short turquoise PLACKET down the centre front carrying two small WHITE buttons; and a turquoise CUFF BAND edged with a fine white line at the end of each short sleeve. Nothing else on it. The club badge sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about three fingers wide: the highfield-herons mark exactly as the crest artwork draws it — a PENNANT flying to the right with the heron's head and long S-curved neck filling it, printed in DARK TEAL. At chest-badge size the pennant reads as a plain triangle coming to a single point on the right: the notched swallowtail fly end of the crest artwork is finer than a printed chest badge can carry, and it must NOT be drawn in as a separate detail here. It is the ONLY mark on the polo. NO maker's logo, NO club name, NO player name, NO number and no lettering of any kind. The BACK of the polo is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it stays PLAIN WHITE: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere on it. Tennis does not number a shirt, and a number across his back would be a mark this polo does not have.
- shorts: PLAIN TURQUOISE tennis SHORTS exactly as photo2.png and photo3.png show them: solid turquoise all over, ending a little above the knee, with a plain elasticated waistband and no stripe, no piping, no side panel and no contrast trim. NO maker's logo, NO number and no lettering on them.
- socks: PLAIN WHITE ANKLE SOCKS, sitting just above the shoe collar, with no stripe, no colour band and no maker's mark, exactly as photo3.png shows them. Not crew socks and not turquoise.
- footwear: PLAIN CREAM-WHITE COURT SHOES exactly as photo3.png shows them after the maker's mark was taken off: a low-profile tennis shoe with pale grey side panels, white laces, a reinforced toe and a flat non-marking herringbone court sole. Completely PLAIN and UNBRANDED — no stripes device, no swoosh, no maker's mark and no lettering anywhere on the upper, and no moulded logo in the heel of the sole either. The same pair in every frame, worn but clean. (art:spec:verify went on reporting a moulded heel logo and side stripes after both were edited out; 4x crops of BOTH shoes in photo3.png — the raised one and the one on his foot — show plain rubber and plain grey overlays. §33: the crop outranks the judge, and this line is not to be reverted on another verifier run.)
- equipment: A PLAIN UNBRANDED RACKET. No ball appears in any photograph; the DECISION is that a plain yellow unbranded tennis ball may appear in a pose where the action needs one, and nowhere else. The racket has a matt black frame with plain white strings. The MATCH racket in photo2.png has a WHITE grip finished with BLACK tape at the top; photo3.png shows a second, different racket lying on the bench with a solid black grip, which is a training-day racket and not this one. The DECISION for every pose is the photo2 racket: black frame, white strings, white grip, black finishing tape. On it there is: NO maker's name, NO model name, NO lettering on the throat, the shaft, the butt cap or the strings. Two small kit items go with it and both are worn: a WHITE terry HEADBAND across the forehead (photo2.png) and a TURQUOISE terry WRISTBAND (photo3.png) — the headband white, the wristband turquoise, both plain and unbranded. The DECISION for the poses is that he carries the racket and nothing else: no kit bag, no bottle, no towel.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about three fingers wide, as photo2.png shows it — a real team badge, not a printed graphic across the front. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

IMAGE 2 SHOWS THIS ATHLETE WEARING THE REAL KIT. You are
photographing THOSE EXACT GARMENTS laid out flat and clean — not designing new
ones in the same colours, and not drawing what the words below describe.

WORK THROUGH THE GARMENT ELEMENT BY ELEMENT AND COPY EACH ONE EXACTLY AS THAT
PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS IT:
- the COLLAR: its shape, its colour, and whether it is laced or plain
- the SLEEVES: their length, and every band or stripe on them — HOW MANY there
  are, how wide each one is, and how far up the arm they sit
- the HEM and any waist band: its colour and its depth
- the BODY of the shirt: its colour, and any panel or piping, or none at all
- the CREST: its size, its shape, its colours and exactly where it sits
- the NUMBER: its colour, its outline, its shape, and every place it appears
- the shorts or pants, the socks and the footwear, the same way

Where the written list and that photograph disagree about how something LOOKS,
the PHOTOGRAPH IS RIGHT and the words are to be ignored. The list only decides
which items belong in the kit, which are branded, and what the photograph does
not show at all.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: the badge sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about three fingers wide, as photo2.png shows it — a real team badge, not a printed graphic across the front. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. Place it exactly there on the shirt as it lies facing you. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- FULL-LENGTH GARMENTS ARE SHOWN AT FULL LENGTH: if the kit includes long trousers or
  pants, lay them out with BOTH legs extended completely straight, hems plainly visible
  at their full distance from the waistband — never folded under, never rolled, never
  cropped by another item, never arranged so they could be mistaken for knee-length.
  The poses copy the garment's LENGTH from this image, exactly like its colour.
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No words anywhere: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no lettering, no woven
  neck label, no care label, no watermark. The squad number appears ONLY if the kit
  description above calls for it, and no other number is invented.
NO REAL-WORLD LEAGUE OR CLUB MARKS, ANYWHERE, EVER. No NFL shield, no NBA, no MLB, no NHL,
no FIFA, no UEFA, no Premier League, no NCAA, no Olympic rings, no national federation
badge, no professional club's crest — not on a jersey, a helmet, a sleeve, a collar, a
label, a ball or a boot, not even small and not even partly hidden. The only badge that
may appear anywhere is the club crest supplied with this request. These emblems carry no
letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
